physics.astrophysics-cosmology-explain-k.all: Big Bang predicts early universe hot/dense; radiation from then has been stretched (redshifted) by expansion into microwaves, uniform from all directions - CMB is that remnant. (Note stem says red-shift.)

physics.astrophysics-cosmology-extended-.b: Universe began from a very small, hot, dense point ~13.8 bn yr ago and has expanded since. Evidence: galaxies' light red-shifted, so receding; more distant galaxies have greater red-shift so moving faster (Hubble) - consistent with expansion from a point; CMB radiation from all directions, remnant of early hot universe, stretched to microwaves.

physics.astrophysics-cosmology-recall-kb.all: red-shift of light from distant galaxies (increasing with distance); cosmic microwave background radiation

physics.astrophysics-stars-describe-kb.0.a: nebula of gas and dust pulled together by gravity; becomes denser/hotter forming protostar; when hot enough hydrogen nuclei fuse - star (main sequence)
physics.astrophysics-stars-describe-kb.0.b: expands to red giant; outer layers shed (planetary nebula), core becomes white dwarf

physics.astrophysics-stars-explain-kb.00.a: inward gravitational force balanced by outward pressure from fusion energy; large hydrogen supply so lasts long
physics.astrophysics-stars-explain-kb.00.b: apparent brightness depends on distance as well as luminosity; a more luminous star further away can look as bright as a dimmer nearer one, so different absolute magnitudes

physics.astrophysics-universe-describe-k.a: universe made of many (billions of) galaxies; each galaxy a large collection of billions of stars (and solar systems)
physics.astrophysics-universe-describe-k.b: moon orbits a planet; planet orbits a star (Sun); different periods/sizes
physics.astrophysics-universe-describe-k.c: mass stays the same; weight decreases (about 1/6) because g on Moon is smaller (1.6 vs 10 N/kg)

physics.astrophysics-universe-explain-kb.a: direction of motion continually changes so velocity changes; acceleration is change of velocity (towards centre, due to gravity)
physics.astrophysics-universe-explain-kb.b: gravitational force from Sun increases as it gets closer; GPE converted to KE
physics.astrophysics-universe-explain-kb.c: gravitational field strength on Moon is lower so weight smaller; same push gives greater height / less deceleration

physics.astrophysics-universe-recall-kb..b: a large collection of billions of stars
physics.astrophysics-universe-recall-kb..c: comet orbit highly elliptical, planet near-circular; comet speed varies greatly / comet orbit not in same plane / longer period
